I'm cautious about another Mass Effect game after the ending of Mass Effect 3.
I know I am in the minority when I say "I really didn't mind it". At worst, I was sad at it ending in general, but I never really understood all the hate that it got?

My main problem with it is twofold: first, the fact that no matter how you played through all 3 games, it really didn't matter what ending you picked, essentially the same thing happens in all 3 scenarios:

  1. The Reapers are no longer hostile (or they're dead)
  2. (In "Destroy" - the canon ending) All the Geth that you may or may not have worked to save from the Quarians are dead (??? - what's the point in allowing us to save them?)
  3. All the Mass Relays are destroyed
  4. The Normandy crashes on some unknown planet
  5. Society rebuilds itself after some unspecified period of time

And second, the sheer number of logical fallacies that existed.

Organics created machines

Machines gained self awareness

Machines started killing organics

Organics created a machine to think of how to deal with the problem, which comes up with:

Create machines to harvest organic life kill the organics when they reach the peak of their civilization (??? - Isn't that the problem you were created to solve?)

Don't bother explaining what you're doing or why, though. Just tell them "You're doomed" and "We will harvest kill you all"

Reapers created, kill all organics (repeated ad nauseum)

Oh by the way, there was this other thing that could have been done had I let the organics live long enough to finish The Catalyst, but I couldn't be arsed /shrugs

In the case of the "Synergy"(?) ending (the one where organics and machines are combined) a third issue crops up: You are forcing a decision you make at the persuasion of an AI that came up with the above ideas upon the entire galaxy regardless of whether or not they like it (or even want it). I'm pretty sure the only being in the main story that benefits directly from that is Joker, since it probably cures his Brittle Bone Disease.

Even when they released the "Expanded" endings I was a bit disappointed, because it didn't fix my main issue with the endings - it just expanded upon the already sucky endings that were there.

  • In the "Control the Reapers" ending, Shepard's physical body is destroyed but he/she becomes the will of the Reapers, using them to prevent wars between machines and organics before they crop up
  • In the "Destroy the Reapers" and "Synergy" endings, nothing was really changed, they just added some exposition
This is a pretty good summary for what's wrong with Mass Effect 3's ending(s), considering there's lots of 30+ minute critique videos on YouTube.
